hints: Find angle $\angle EAB$ using right triangle $\triangle ABE$ with $\tan(\angle EAB) = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$.
Subtract $2\angle EAB$ from the corner right angle $\frac{\pi}{2}$ to find $\angle EAF$.
walkthrough:
Calculate angle $\angle EAB$ in right triangle $\triangle ABE$ with $AB = 12$ and $BE = 4$:
$$\tan(\angle EAB) = \frac{BE}{AB} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3} \implies \angle EAB = \arctan\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \approx 0.32175\text{ rad}$$

Subtract both corner angles from the corner right angle $\angle BAD = \frac{\pi}{2}$ to find $\angle EAF$:
$$\angle EAF = \frac{\pi}{2} - 2\arctan\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \approx 1.57080 - 0.64350 = 0.927295 \approx 0.9273\text{ radians (to 4 s.f.)}$$

hints: Find straight sides $EC = FC = 12 - 4 = 8\text{ cm}$ and circular arc length $r\theta = \sqrt{160}(0.9273)$.
Add $EC + FC + \text{Arc } EF$ to find the total perimeter.
walkthrough:
Calculate the radius of the circular arc $r = AE$ using Pythagoras' Theorem on $\triangle ABE$:
$$r = AE = \sqrt{12^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{144 + 16} = \sqrt{160} \approx 12.6491\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the lengths of the straight boundaries $EC$ and $FC$:
$$EC = 12 - 4 = 8\text{ cm}, \quad FC = 12 - 4 = 8\text{ cm}$$

Compute the circular arc length of arc $EF$:
$$\text{Arc } EF = r\theta = \sqrt{160} \times 0.9273 \approx 11.7295\text{ cm}$$

Sum all boundary components to find the perimeter of the shaded region:
$$\text{Perimeter} = EC + FC + \text{Arc } EF = 8 + 8 + 11.7295 = 27.7295 \approx 27.7\text{ cm (to 3 s.f.)}$$

hints: Calculate the area of square $ABCD = 12^2 = 144\text{ cm}^2$.
Calculate areas of triangles $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle ADF$: $2 \times \frac{1}{2}(12)(4) = 48\text{ cm}^2$.
Calculate sector area $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(160)(0.9273)$, and subtract all from the square area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of the total square $ABCD$:
$$\text{Area}(ABCD) = 12 \times 12 = 144\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the areas of the two unshaded corner right triangles $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle ADF$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ABE) = \frac{1}{2}(12)(4) = 24\text{ cm}^2, \quad \text{Area}(\triangle ADF) = \frac{1}{2}(12)(4) = 24\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the area of circular sector $AEF$ with $r^2 = 160$ and $\theta = 0.9273\text{ rad}$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Sector } AEF) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(160)(0.927295) = 74.1836\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the two triangles and the sector from the square area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 144 - 24 - 24 - 74.1836 = 96 - 74.1836 = 21.8164 \approx 21.8\text{ cm}^2 \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
